check.reason: The take states 'Nearly 40% of advisory committee meetings over 20 years' as fact. Nothing in the real headline supports that figure or time span, and the rules prohibit inventing numbers. Unless the 40% and 20-year figures appear verbatim in the source summary, remove them or use a non-numeric phrase such as 'a large share of meetings.' The rest passes. The target is the system (pharma funding and FDA process), patients are treated as the ones being failed, no reporter is mocked, nothing is quoted, and the tone is dry and deadpan.

pick.title: Many patient, consumer reps on FDA advisory panels have ties to groups funded by pharma, analysis finds
pick.headline: FDA Panels Hear From Patients Through Generous Support of Pharmaceutical Industry
pick.take: Nearly 40% of advisory committee meetings over 20 years included a patient or consumer rep tied to an advocacy group that pharma funds. The sponsor presents the data and helps underwrite the group that responds to it. Patients deserve a seat at the table that nobody else is paying for.
